Criminal Petition 6443/2022 is filed by the petitioner accused Nos.1 and 2 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR in Crime No.58/2021 registered by Basavanaudi Police, Bangalore, for the offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of IPC on the complaint filed by M.G.
Vijaya Kumar, the 2nd respondent herein.

2. Criminal Petition No.6339/2022 is filed by petitioner sole accused (petitioner No.1 in Criminal Petition No.6443/2022) under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing FIR in Crime No.20/2022 registered by Basavanagudi Police, Bangalore, for the offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of IPC on the complaint filed by Y.A. Narasimha Murthy, the 2nd respondent herein.

Writ Petition No.13715/2022 is filed by the M.G. Vijaya Kumar, (Respondent No.2 in Criminal Petition No.6443/2022) under Articles 226 and 227 of Constitution of India read with Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the order dated 07.06.2022 passed by the Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore in Crime No.20/2022 and for a direction to issue the mandamus to respondent No.4- Manager, Bank of Maharashtra, not to defreeze/transfer the amount which was lien freezed sum of Rs.80.00 lakhs seized in Crime No.58/2021.
4.

The case of the petitioner-accused Nos.1 and 2 in criminal petition No.6443/2022 is that on the complaint filed by M.G. Vijaya Kumar, on 08.03.2021 against the petitioner-accused Nos.1 and 2 before the Basavanagudi police, the policed registered the case.

It is alleged that the petitioner-accused Nos.1-Tirumalai and accused No.2- Saraswathi Tirumalai entered into a rental agreement on 04.06.2020 by receiving Rs.80.00 lakhs by cheuqe for letting out their house No.9,
situated at 3rd Lane, Tata Silk Farm, Basavanagudi, but they refused to give the house on rent and they also refused to return the advance amount paid by the complainant to them.
The accused gave false promise to return the same and they also threatened with dire consequences.

It is further stated in the complaint that on 02.02.2021, the first accused Tirumalai came to the Police station and agreed to settle the issue by repaying Rs.35.00 lakhs by 28.02.2021 and the balance with interest by 31.03.2021, but he has not paid till date and he has willfully cheated the complainant and hence, prayed for taking the action.
The police on receiving the complaint, registered the case against the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 and investigating the matter, which is under challenge.

5. The facts of the case of very same petitioner No.1-Tirumalai in Criminal Petition No.6339/2022 is that one Y.A. Narasimha Murthy filed a complaint to the police 24.01.2022 alleging that the petitioner said to be the owner of M/s. Trans India Estate and Developers and on 12.12.2007, the complainant and one Narayan formed a firm namely, N&N Land Developers and Builders for formation of layout intended for members of friends circle.

They finalized with the petitioner for acquisition and development of layout and entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with Jyothi Velu, the owner of Vinu Developers as confirmed party to act as liaison to procure and develop the layout.
On 04.02.2021, initial location for layout formation was identified at Adigarakallahalli, Sarjapur.
Around 400 members, permitted to go ahead with project.
The members were intimated to pay initial deposit for making advance amount to the petitioner, who is the owner of M/s. Trans India Estate and Developers, to start the project.
The interested members started making initial deposit in favour of the complainant and a sum of Rs.18,64,30,000/- were raised from more than 400 members.

From October 2009 to June 2011, advance of Rs.14,78,00,000/- was paid in installments to developer for land procurement and development,
through cheques as well as cash.
On 10.11.2010, 4 acres 29 guntas of converted land at Adigarakallahalli, Sarjapur, was registered in favour of N&N Developers by the petitioner- Tiumalai.
After registration of 4 acres 29 guntas of land, there was no progress in the development and the members were desired to withdraw application for allotment of sites and demanded for refund.
The developer agreed to refund and issued cheques for Rs.3,85,00,000/- from February, 2012 to August 2012 and the said cheques got bounced.

On 27.06.2012, the developer (Trans India) written a letter to the complainant communicating payment of Rs.1,83,90,000/- and the balance of Rs.12,69,10,000/- would be paid back subject to cancellation of Memorandum of Understanding.

sentences.text:
It is further alleged that on 18.08.2012, the developer was informed about dishonour of cheques,
but no action was initiated by the complainant company as the petitioner agreed to make alternate arrangement for payment.

In the meanwhile, to mobilize the fund for refund to the members, 4.29 acres of land stood in the name of complainant company was sold on 23.02.2013 and the proceeds were used for refund of deposit amount of few members.
Additionally, his personal property was also pledged and refunds were made to the members to the tune of Rs.1.08 crores.
On regular follow up, the developer made payment for refund of sum of Rs.2.34 crores during the period from 2013 to 2016.
It is also alleged in the complaint that the complainant undergone open heart surgery and he was forced to form a new partnership with Tirumalai and Jyothi Velu on 07.11.2016 without his willingness.
The developer came forward to take up 2-3 new site visits for the remaining members.
They were not happy with location and requested for refund.
The developer falsely promised to refund but there was no concrete commitment from the petitioner-accused.
7. It is further alleged that the total amount Rs.14.78 crores was paid to the petitioner and the petitioner repaid Rs.5.20 crores, but Rs.9.58 crores is still pending.
The petitioner is not responding to the calls and messages.
On visiting house of the petitioner, the building was seized by the Bank of Maharashtra and he was untraceable.
He is not in a position to refund the amount.
More than 130 members have invested along with the complainant.
Hence, prayed for taking action.
After receipt of the complaint, the police registered FIR in Crime No.20/2022 which is under challenge by the petitioner- accused in this petition.
8. Whereas, Writ Petition No.13715/2022 is filed by M.G. Vijaya Kumar against the accused-Tirumalai, to quash the order dated 07.06.2022 in Crime No.20/2022 passed by the Sessions Judge.

It is alleged that accused- Tirumalai, (respondent No.3 in this case) and his wife Saraswathi executed rental agreement in favour of writ petitioner under the registered document dated 04.06.2020 and received Rs.15.00 lakhs through RTGS and Rs.35.00 lakhs by cheque from petitioner's wife and another Rs. 30.00 lakhs by cheque of petitioner, totally, Rs.80.00 lakhs for letting out the house situated at No.5, 3rd Lane, Tata Silk Farm, Basavanagudi, Bangalore, and they have not given the possession of the house and also not repaid the amount.
Thereby, the respondent No.3- accused cheated the writ petitioner-complainant.
During investigation, the police issued notice to the Bank of Maharastra by freezing the account of accused in A/c. No.68016120281 and a lien freeze was made in respect of account of the accused.
Thereafter, the Basavanagudi police transferred case to Jayanagar police for further investigation.
9. It is further contended that one more complaint is filed by one Y.A. Narasimha Murthy against the accused- Tirumalai on 24.01.2022 for cheating under Section 420 read with Section 34 of IPC.
Subsequently, Section 9 of Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004 (for short 'KPID Act') has been invoked.

entities.text: Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Basavanagudi police issued a notice to Bank of Maharastra and freezed the account of the Tirumalai.

He further contended that Narasimha Murhty, i.e. the complainant in Crime No.20/2022 also filed an application under Section 451 and 457 of Cr.P.C. for releasing the amount of Rs.1.42 crores from the freezed account of respondent No.3-Tirumalai.
The Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore, ordered to release the amount by defreezing the account.

entities.text: Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner herein also filed an application in his complaint before the Magistrate for defreezing the account and release of amount of Rs.80.00 lakhs Tirumalai B R vs The State By on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186054084/
6 from the account of accused-Tirumalai and the XXXVII Metropolitan Magistrate also passed an order directing the bank authorities to release Rs.80.00 lakhs in favour of the petitioner.
10.

entities.text: Tirumalai B R vs The State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner contended that respondent No.2 by suppressing the fact, obtained the order before the Sessions Judge, and therefore, the Sessions Judge also passed an order directing the release of Rs.1.40 crores in favour of respondent No.2 which includes the amount belongs to the petitioner.
Hence, prayed for allowing the petition.
11. Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, perused the records.

12. On perusal of the records, in respect of criminal Petition No.6443/2022 where accused Nos.1 and 2 are the petitioners in respect of crime No.58/21 on the complaint filed by Vijaya Kumar (respondent No.2), wherein it is alleged that respondent No.2 Vijaya Kumar has paid Rs.80.00 lakhs for obtaining the house of the petitioner for rent, but the petitioners by receiving the amount by transfer, have not given the house to the respondent- complainant for occupation or not refunded the lease amount.
Therefore, Vijaya Kumar filed the complaint.

The police freezed the account of the petitioner and subsequently, the said complainant filed an application for release of the amount freezed by the police which was ordered by XXXVII Magistrate for release of 80.00 lakhs.

In the meanwhile, the petitioner-accused is also involved in Crime No.20/2022 registered by Basavanagudi police for cheating the crores of rupees received from Narasimha Murthy, who is a builder in respect of Memorandum of Understanding for developing the land and giving sites to the members.

Due to the said dispute, a complaint was filed by Narasimha Murthy and in view of invoking KPID Act against the petitioner-accused, the matter is pending before the Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore, where once again the Jayanagar Police freezed the same account belongs to the accused at Bank of Maharashtra, wherein the very Narasimha Murthy also filed a similar application for releasing the amount of Rs.1,41,00,000/- in the account of the accused which was freezed by the police.

entities.text: Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In other words, the amount of Rs.1,41,00,000/- was available in the account of Tirumalai at the Bank of Maharashtra and the same was attached by Basavanagudi police and Jayanagar police.

During investigation, two FIRS registered by the same Basavanagudi police against same accused on two different complaints filed by one Vijaya Kumar for Rs.80.00 lakhs and Narasimha Murthy for more than Rs.9.00 crores for cheating.

13. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner-accused in Criminal Petition No.6339/2022 is that the dispute between the parties is civil in nature and the respondents have given the colour of criminality, they can file the suit for recovery before the Commercial Court, etc.

But, on perusal of the records in Crime No.20/2022, there was Memorandum of Understanding between two developers and more than Rs.14.00 crores was received by the accused for developing the land, but not materialized and a case was filed.
Now the investigation was taken up by the Jayanagar police and they invoked KPID Act in respect of Crime No.20/2022.
The accused cheated various members by receiving the amount and the crores of public money was involved.
The matter requires detailed investigation by the police.
Even under the KPID Act, the Assistant Commissioner also requires to be appointed to protect the interest of the investors.
Such being the case, the question of quashing FIR in Crime No.20/2022 challenged in Criminal Petition No.6339/2022 cannot be allowed.
The matter requires detailed investigation and the police are required to make detail investigation.

Tirumalai B R vs The State By on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186054084/
7

entities.text: Tirumalai B R vs The State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petition filed by the petitioner-accused in W.P.No.6339/2022 challenging the FIR in Crime No.20/2022 is liable to be dismissed.

14. Whereas, in Criminal Petition No.6443/2022, the cheating case was registered against accused Nos.1 and 2 (husband and wife) for receiving Rs.80.00 lakhs from the complainant under registered agreement, but neither the house was given for rent nor the amount was refunded by the accused.

It is also seen from the records that the complainant has already fled a civil suit in O.S.
No.26204/2021 before the Civil Judge, Bangalore, for recovery of Rs.85.00 lakhs including the court fee and also for a direction to the bank to satisfy the lien account of the 1st defendant therein,
who is the accused herein.

The lease agreement was also produced before the Court by the petitioner which reveals that if any dispute arose between the lessor and lessee, the matter shall be referred to a sole arbitrator for conciliation.

On perusal of these two documents, it reveals that the lease agreement provides a clause at Sl. No.16, that if any dispute arise between the parties, the dispute shall be referred to the sole arbitrator for arbitration and conciliation.
That apart, the complainant has also already filed a civil suit in O.S. No.26204/2021 for recovering of the lease amount of Rs.80.00 lakhs from the petitioner-accused.

Therefore, it clearly reveals that if any dispute arose between the parties, it would be civil in nature and the complainant has already invoked the civil court for recovery of the lease amount paid by him.
Such being the case, the question of filing complaint is nothing but recovery of the amount in Crime No.58/2021.
Therefore, the FIR in Crime No.58/2021 is liable to be quashed as the dispute between the parties is civil in nature.

Hence,
Criminal Petition No.6443/2022 is liable to be allowed.

15. As regards to Writ Petition No.13715/2022 filed by the same complainant-Vijaya Kumar for modification of the order dated 07.06.2022 passed by the Sessions Judge in Crime No.20/2022 for freezing the account and payment of Rs.80 lakhs ordered by the Magistrate, on perusal of the both orders passed by the Magistrate and Sessions Judge in both Crime Nos.20/2022 and 58/2021 by different complainants, this Court has already held that the complaint filed against the petitioner in Crime No.58/2021 for refund of lease amount and cheating the complainant, he has already approached the Civil Court and there is already an arbitration clause in the agreement.
Hence, the FIR cannot be sustained and liable to be quashed.

Therefore, the petitioner-complainant is not entitled for Rs.80 lakhs which is freezed by the police in Crime No.58/2021, on the other hand, the Sessions Judge has already freezed the account of the accused in crime No.20/2022 under the KPID Act, which is already released to the complainant Narasimha Murthy of N&N Developers.
This amount belongs to the various investors and the Sessions Judge has already de-
freezed the account and ordered to release to the complainant Narasimha Murthy.
Such being the case, the question of setting aside the order of Sessions Judge does not arise.
Therefore, the writ petition filed by the petitioner-complainant is liable to be dismissed.

16. Accordingly, I pass the following order:
(i) Criminal petition filed by the petitioner-sole accused in Criminal Petition No.6339/2022 arising out of crime No.20/2022 registered by Basavanagudi police,
now pending on the file of Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore, is hereby dismissed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
During investigation, the police issued notice to the Bank of Maharastra by freezing the account of accused in A/c. No.68016120281 and a lien freeze was made in respect of account of the accused.
Thereafter, the Basavanagudi police transferred case to Jayanagar police for further investigation.
9. It is further contended that one more complaint is filed by one Y.A. Narasimha Murthy against the accused- Tirumalai on 24.01.2022 for cheating under Section 420 read with Section 34 of IPC.
Subsequently, Section 9 of Karnataka Protection of Interest of Depositors in Financial Establishments Act, 2004 (for short 'KPID Act') has been invoked.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
13. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner-accused in Criminal Petition No.6339/2022 is that the dispute between the parties is civil in nature and the respondents have given the colour of criminality, they can file the suit for recovery before the Commercial Court, etc.
The accused cheated various members by receiving the amount and the crores of public money was involved.
Tirumalai B R vs The State By on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186054084/
7
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Now the investigation was taken up by the Jayanagar police and they invoked KPID Act in respect of Crime No.20/2022.
Even under the KPID Act, the Assistant Commissioner also requires to be appointed to protect the interest of the investors.
Such being the case, the question of quashing FIR in Crime No.20/2022 challenged in Criminal Petition No.6339/2022 cannot be allowed.
Therefore, it clearly reveals that if any dispute arose between the parties, it would be civil in nature and the complainant has already invoked the civil court for recovery of the lease amount paid by him.
Such being the case, the question of filing complaint is nothing but recovery of the amount in Crime No.58/2021.
Therefore, the FIR in Crime No.58/2021 is liable to be quashed as the dispute between the parties is civil in nature.
Hence,
Criminal Petition No.6443/2022 is liable to be allowed.
Hence, the FIR cannot be sustained and liable to be quashed.
Therefore, the petitioner-complainant is not entitled for Rs.80 lakhs which is freezed by the police in Crime No.58/2021, on the other hand, the Sessions Judge has already freezed the account of the accused in crime No.20/2022 under the KPID Act, which is already released to the complainant Narasimha Murthy of N&N Developers.
opennyai_summary.decision:
This amount belongs to the various investors and the Sessions Judge has already de-
freezed the account and ordered to release to the complainant Narasimha Murthy.
Such being the case, the question of setting aside the order of Sessions Judge does not arise.
Therefore, the writ petition filed by the petitioner-complainant is liable to be dismissed.
16. Accordingly, I pass the following order:
(i) Criminal petition filed by the petitioner-sole accused in Criminal Petition No.6339/2022 arising out of crime No.20/2022 registered by Basavanagudi police,
now pending on the file of Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore, is hereby dismissed.
The FIR in Crime No.58/2021 registered by Basavanagudi police for the offence punishable under Section 420 read with Section 34 of IPC is hereby allowed and the FIR in Crime No.58/2021 is quashed.
(iii) Consequently, Writ Petition No.13715/2022 filed by the complainant-Vijaya Kumar challenging the order dated 07.06.2022 passed by the Principal City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bangalore, in Crime No.20/2022 is hereby dismissed.
